text.p: Following are some of the leading stories in Russian newspapers this morning. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
SEVODNYA
- Russia and Belarus are not likely to sign any crucial documents on May 23.
- The recent confrontation with the State Duma proved that the government is a united team.
- Kemero, Russia's biggest mining region, is on the edge of social unrest.
- Foreign loans are not being used efficiently, the Audit Chamber of the Russian Federation says.
KOMMERSANT DAILY
- Chechen authorities are not interested in finding Russian journalists kidnapped in the breakaway republic, Russian special services think.
- As Russia is trying to define relations with NATO, Ukraine has intensified ties with the former Soviet Baltic republics.
- Russia's Central Bank expressed its concern over changes on the international currency market caused by the introduction of a common European currency
- The State Duma lower house of the Russian parliament is in serious conflict with the government over budget-cutting plans.
- Deutsche Bank is to open its subsidiary in Moscow.
- Russia, which offers two thirds of a world palladium supplies, can create real crisis on a world market.
NEZAVISIMAYA GAZETA
- Prime Minister Viktor Chernomyrdin's speech in parliament proved that the much advertised presidential plan to improve the country's economic and social situation is unrealistic.
- On the eve of signing of a new document defining relations between Russia and Belarus, enthusiasm over unification with Moscow has calmed down in Minsk.
ROSSIISKAYA GAZETA
- The discussion on the budget cuts in the State Duma yesterday looked like a dialogue between representatives of different civilisations using different languages.
SOVIETSKAYA ROSSIA
- Only radical change of the (political and economic) course can improve the situation in the country, says the leader of communist opposition Gennady Zyuganov.
KOMSOMOLSKAYA PRAVDA
- The Founding Act on Russia and NATO relations facilitates avoiding of confrontation between the two parties, said Russia's Foreign Minister Yevgeny Primakov.
-- Svetlana Kovaleva, Moscow Newsroom, +7095 941 8520
